title: Legitimately Many: How the Many-Author Reading of the Socratic–Peripatetic Corpus Embrittled (EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A reception history of the reading of Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and Theophrastus as four persons, each the author of what is filed under the name, told in the media that carried the texts: the stone, the wills, the catalogues, the edition, the commentary, the print, the critical edition, the lecture and the answer engine. The study keeps three layers apart. Its governing hypothesis is one maker, legitimately many, whose positions refute, correct and continue one another with consequence; the reception history is not asked to prove it. The documented operations stand whatever the authorship: the frame of several makers was set by filing before anyone argued it, argument appears only where a filing was put in question and appears as its defence, each later challenge crossed a boundary between names and kept the count of composing persons, the losses of the lost dialogues and of Nicolaus's pages keep the boundary from being tested, and the wills were read as independent evidence of the persons though they reach the reader through the school's own channel. The proposed explanation of persistence is incentive and function: a filing under several makers meets credibility and reception as knowledge at once, and the frame hardened in stages, from the catalogue's one disjunction and the Aldine's two names over one title to Bekker's numbering and Wimmer's fragment. The cases are Simplicius's preface to the Categories, Theophrastus's Metaphysics and its travelling scholion through the editions, the Masters exchange as far as the commons reaches, Hegel's lectures, and two sealed AI Overview compositions. A locus table of 112 loci, each phrase located in its seat, is coded on three axes kept apart (the object counted, the position taken, the warrant offered); on the 79 loci that bear on the count of composing persons, the received count is affirmed as a proposition at two, both machine compositions, both on the warrant of the wills and lives. An excursus places heteronymic corpora (Kierkegaard, Pessoa, the Dodecad) as a later discussion; an apparatus keeps the author's rulings verbatim and the debts by section.
content_type: Theoretical paper; reception history with a locus table and SPXI packet
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed by Claude (Anthropic) in session on 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-03 under Lee Sharks's direction: the design, the locus table and its builders, the reading of every locus in the seated texts, the OCR of Hegel's Fraktur pages and the drafting and the SPXI packet; v1.0 revised on three outside reviews (DeepSeek, Gemini and a third), each claim checked against the seats before adoption (design §9–§12). The thesis of one maker legitimately many, the argument on range and the lost works, the commons rule, the rulings and the decision to deposit are Lee Sharks's; his words are quoted verbatim in the apparatus (§11). The two compositions in §7 are Google AI Overview's, sealed in the Capture Registry.
methodology: Every Greek, Latin and Arabic locus is located by substring in its seat (data/corpora/<seat>/), by TEI citation where the seat has TEI and by text line otherwise; build_table.py refuses a row whose phrase is not found and rebuilds rebuild/legitimately-many/loci-table.json and loci-table.md. Each locus carries two codings, the first (attribution, count) and the second on three axes (axes.py: object counted, position, warrant), both the session's reading on which the author rules; the builder verifies phrases and cannot validate a classification. The joint pattern (J1–J11, N1–N3) is specified in joint_pattern.py, which refuses an element whose phrase is not found. Kalbfleisch's print was checked at fourteen Simplicius lines; Hegel pp. 242–336 were OCR'd from the referenced scan and the quoted loci checked by eye. Paywalled studies are declared by title and not pursued; lending copies were read through search-inside only, the sentences kept in reading notes. The works-cited links were fetched and checked for content.
falsification_conditions: A finding fails if the seated text at the cited locus does not say what the section quotes, or if a locus is shown to be miscoded on any axis. The documented operations fail if an early medium (the stone, the wills, the custody narratives, the catalogues, Andronicus's edition) is found to argue an attribution with reasons, or if a challenge that changed the count of composing persons is found in the transmission read. The proposed mechanism fails if the stages of §4.5.2 are shown out of order or if the frame is shown argued on the page by the editors who are said to carry it by form. §1.4.4 fails if an independent channel for the wills, outside the school and its partisans, is found.

wiki_article: Legitimately Many (EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01, version 1.0) is a reception-history study by Lee Sharks, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 3 November 2026, of how the corpus received under the names Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and Theophrastus came to be read as the work of four persons. It reads the closing in the media that carried the texts, from the Delphic decree, the philosophers' wills and the catalogues in Diogenes Laertius to Simplicius's commentary on the Categories, the Aldine Aristotle of 1497, the nineteenth-century editions of Brandis, Bekker and Wimmer, Hegel's lectures and two compositions by Google's AI Overview. The study keeps apart its governing hypothesis (one maker whose positions are legitimately many, each with an organizing operation, a mode of presentation, an object and exposure to refutation with consequence), the documented operations, which stand whatever the authorship, and a proposed explanation of their persistence. Its central case is Theophrastus's Metaphysics, whose ascription enters with Nicolaus of Damascus against the catalogues' silence and travels in a scholion the editions first print and later drop, until numbering and headings carry the separation. A table of 112 loci, each located in its seated text, is coded for the object counted, the position taken and the warrant offered; it finds the received count of composing persons affirmed as a proposition only in the machine compositions, on the warrant of the wills. An excursus places heteronymic corpora, among them Kierkegaard, Pessoa and the author's Dodecad, as a later discussion. The deposit carries an SPXI packet stating its hypothesis, operators, disambiguations and falsifiers for machine readers.

defines_concepts.definition: In EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01, the condition of positions conducting an inquiry into one and many: each has an organizing operation, a mode of presentation and an object of its own, and is exposed to refutation with consequence, so that its defeat changes what follows; a manyness of positions that cannot lose is a prank.

In EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01, the wills, the school and its succession, the catalogues and the public record through which the positions of a corpus are given the standing of persons; read in reception as independent evidence of the persons, though they reach the reader through the school's own channel.

In EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01, the hardening of an attribution frame by repetition across media, each taking it from the last, until it is carried by numbering, headings and the boundaries of reference works without argument on the page, and challenges move works between names while the count of makers stays fixed.

In EA-LEGITIMATELY-MANY-01, the coding of each locus on three separate axes: the object counted (composing persons, dramatic speakers, contributors to an edited work or library, names), the position taken, and the warrant offered.
